name: Royal Cafe
why_it_matters: Opened 1991 by the three Ahuja brothers — credited with inventing the basket chaat (a deep-fried potato-julienne basket loaded with tikki, chickpeas, dahi and chutneys). Hardayal Maurya, a long-time chef, is the city's named creator of the dish.
insider_tip: The basket chaat travels poorly — eat in. Sahara Ganj branch on Shahnajaf Road is roomier; the original Mahatma Gandhi Road outlet is more cramped but has the brand's better-rated ratings.
signature_address: 9/7, Shahnajaf Road, opposite Sahara Ganj Mall, Hazratganj, Lucknow 226001

name: Sharma Ji Ki Chai
why_it_matters: Founded 1949 by Shri Om Prakash Sharma — third-generation now. Endorsed by UP Tourism, photographed by every food writer who's worked Lucknow. Bun makkhan (a pav split open and stuffed with churned white butter) plus the kulhad chai is the canonical breakfast.
insider_tip: The Lalbagh shop near Darul Shafa is the original; a Hazratganj-area satellite operates separately. Mornings are crowded with politicians and journalists — go before 9am or after 11.
signature_address: 4633, Behind Darul Shafa, TN Road, Lalbagh, Lucknow 226001

name: Naushijaan
why_it_matters: Hazratganj's go-to for the full kebab roster in one sitting — kakori, galouti, majlisi (originally designed for large-group serving on earthen platters). Cleaner setting than the Chowk legends, easier for first-time travellers.
insider_tip: Order the majlisi kebab if you're in a group — it's plated for sharing. Mornings the kitchen is slower; the kebab quality peaks 7-9pm.

name: Moti Mahal
why_it_matters: Long-running pure-veg counter on MG Road in the heart of Hazratganj — chaat and mithai downstairs, casual dine-in upstairs. Imarti drowned in saffron rabdi is the dessert locals are nostalgic about.
insider_tip: Skip the menu and ask for whatever's freshest at the chaat counter; the kitchen's strength is street-food assembly, not the upstairs Mughlai. No connection to the Delhi 'Moti Mahal Delux' butter-chicken brand.
